label: Self-released
description: Hazel City's quiet debut, nine plainspoken songs of home-recorded acoustic guitar and layered vocal harmonies. It plays like a diary of a Rust Belt hometown, unhurried and intimate rather than showy.
lineage: A Gary, Indiana bedroom-folk project that grew out of the same Bandcamp DIY networks as Chicago's indie-folk scene, laying groundwork for the fuller-band goblynmarkytt.

label: Self-released
description: A nine-song set built around memorable, unfussy melodies and a rotating cast of guest vocalists, giving these hushed folk songs a communal, porch-session feel rather than a solo-singer-songwriter one.
lineage: Continues the plainspoken small-town folk of Old Friend with a wider circle of collaborators, part of the 2020s wave of Bandcamp-first indie-folk acts Josh Terry has tracked at No Expectations.

label: No Quarter
description: Recorded in a friend's upstate New York barn, this is spare, unhurried folk built from a repeating image of a bird hitting a window; Horn's guitarist trades quiet call-and-response lines with her plainspoken vocal across ten dreamlike songs.
lineage: Grew out of Horn's Austin songwriting circle and a period studying poetry; No Quarter also houses Joan Shelley, placing Horn in the same lineage of hushed, literary indie folk.

label: Self-released
description: Horn's self-titled follow-up is minimalist to the point of near-silence in places, sparse guitar figures under scalpel-precise, evocative lyric fragments; a dreamy, unhurried record that rewards close listening.
lineage: A further distillation of the hushed, literary style she developed on The Window Is The Dream.

album: It's Summer, I Love You, and I'm Surrounded by Snow
label: Self-released
description: Geneviève Beaudoin's twelve-song set swings her voice from a warble to a coo to a full scream over dark, romantic, disorienting folk arrangements; a breakup and self-reckoning record that never settles into one register for long.
lineage: Part of the Portland, Maine DIY folk scene alongside Lily Seabird's circle; Terry compared the impact of Beaudoin's voice here to first hearing Angel Olsen's Burn Your Fire.

label: Saddle Creek
description: Meg Duffy's most ambitious Hand Habits record to date, produced by Sasami Ashworth; folk-rooted songwriting opened up into lusher, more adventurous arrangements after a pandemic-forced pause, with Perfume Genius guesting on one track.
lineage: Duffy came up as an in-demand guitarist for Kevin Morby and War on Drugs before Hand Habits' own records; Fun House marks the point where the project moved from insular bedroom folk toward fuller studio arrangements.

label: Fat Possum Records
description: A love record shadowed by quiet anxiety, veering from insular early Hand Habits songwriting toward a fuzzier, 90s-indebted guitar-rock feel in the vein of Aimee Mann or Neko Case, with occasional horns and Wurlitzer.
lineage: Follows Fun House's move outward from Duffy's solo bedroom style, made as Duffy also became a full-time member of Perfume Genius's touring band.

label: Self-released
description: A Seattle bassist-singer's rich, lush-voiced solo debut of organically arranged folk songs, quiet and confident in its plainspoken storytelling.
lineage: Blackwell is primarily a bassist and guitarist in the Seattle scene; My Maze established her as a songwriter in her own right before Dream a Day.

label: Self-released
description: Ten warm, unhurried songs continuing Blackwell's plainspoken songwriting, self-released between her debut and the more widely noticed Dream a Day.
lineage: A bridge record between My Maze and Dream a Day, part of Blackwell's steady, independent Bandcamp release schedule.

label: Self-released
description: A rich, lush-voiced set of thirteen organically arranged folk songs, self-released only on Bandcamp; Blackwell's most fully realized record to date.
lineage: The culmination of Blackwell's run of independent Seattle folk records, released as her profile grew beyond her session-musician reputation.

album: I Need to Start a Garden
label: Mama Bird Recording Co.
description: Heynderickx's debut is conversational, fingerpicked folk that finds grace in the mundane, from housework to horticulture, sung in a voice that can turn from a murmur to a full-throated cry within a verse.
lineage: Emerged from Portland's DIY folk circuit; the record's patient, plainspoken observation set a template picked up by later Mama Bird and Fat Possum-adjacent songwriters like Lily Seabird.

label: Mama Bird Recording Co.
description: Ten verdant, conversational songs continuing the plainspoken observation of her debut, finding quiet grace in ordinary domestic and natural detail across a patient, guitar-centered record.
lineage: A six-years-later follow-up to I Need to Start a Garden, made after Heynderickx spent the interim touring and collaborating, including on the Max García Conover duo record.

label: Fat Possum Records
description: A duo record rooted in Woody Guthrie and radical folk history, nuanced protest songs traded between two plainspoken, patient singer-guitarists.
lineage: Connects Heynderickx's Portland folk lineage to Maine songwriter Max García Conover's own Woody Guthrie-indebted catalog.

label: Transgressive / Liberation / Polyvinyl
description: Jacklin's debut pairs a plainspoken alto with spare, twang-tinged arrangements, coming-of-age songs about leaving small-town New South Wales that sit closer to country-folk than to polished pop.
lineage: Grew from Melbourne's singer-songwriter scene; set up the more countryish overlap with Core sound that would surface fully on Pre Pleasure.
borderline_note: Debut leans closer to plain singer-songwriter pop than later records; kept in C5 per field-guide mapping.

label: Transgressive / Liberation / Polyvinyl
description: A breakup record about bodily autonomy and the end of a long relationship, delivered in Jacklin's plain, unadorned voice over spare full-band arrangements that lean acoustic more than electric.
lineage: Widely cited alongside Maple Glider and Stella Donnelly as part of a wave of Australian songwriters mining plainspoken, folk-rooted heartbreak writing.

label: Transgressive / Liberation / Polyvinyl
description: Jacklin's most overtly twang-inflected record, with clean electric guitar and horns wrapped around wry, closely observed songs about love, faith and self-image.
lineage: The clearest overlap between Jacklin's pop-folk songwriting and Core's twangy indie-folk sound, cited by Terry alongside Maple Glider's I Get Into Trouble as a touchstone.
borderline_note: Pop/indie artist's country-adjacent turn; kept in C5 (rather than Context) because the twang texture is explicit here, per brief guidance.

note: Released 25 September 2026 (day of research); confirmed via Wikipedia and Bandcamp (label 4AD) but no track titles could be confirmed from a scraped page in time.

album: Now Would Be A Good Time
label: Jagjaguwar
description: Three former high-school friends trade dazzling three-part harmonies over acoustic-led arrangements, wry and darkly funny songs about breakups, dissociation and modern early-twenties life.
lineage: Signed to Jagjaguwar (Bon Iver, Angel Olsen, Sharon Van Etten), the trio toured with Julia Jacklin and sit close to her and Stella Donnelly in the current Australian indie-folk wave.
